what:
speed-sol-core (lane core's speed of light): the daemon's plane loop pays three shared atomic round trips and a channel block per task.

Where: crates/blaze-cargo/src/serve/plane.rs, `Threads::new` (lines ~219-220), `post_work` (~278-301), `Threads::post` (~304-313), and the two `batch.work.clone()` at ~604 and ~703.

What it costs: per task posted, the loop thread does `batch.work.clone()` (Arc increment), `self.done_tx.clone()` (crossbeam Sender count increment), and `post_work` does `again = work.clone()` (another Arc increment); the worker drops all three (three decrements). Each of those six RMWs is on one of two lines every task shares (the `W` Arc's count, the channel's sender count), so on a 64-core build each is a cross-core miss: about 6 x 100 ns = 0.6 us of the loop thread and the workers per task. Against the warm-build bound in docs/v2/plan/lanes/core/speed-of-light.md (1,000,000 cache hits of 2 us on 64 cores: 31 ms, under 0.2 us of overhead a task), that alone is 3x the budget. Also `done` and `io` are `unbounded()` channels: crossbeam's list flavor allocates a 31-slot block every 31 sends, on the sender (a worker) and frees on the receiver.

The edit (what lane core's `exec::Scheduler` does, crates/blaze-graph/src/exec.rs `Ctx`/`drive`):
1. Keep what every task of a `Threads` shares in one context made once and leaked, or owned by `Threads` and outliving its jobs: the `W` (instead of an `Arc<W>` per batch) and the `done` sender. Pass `&'static Ctx<W>` (a Copy reference) into `run`/`then`; `again` and the give-way re-post use the same reference; nothing is cloned per task. If `W` must stay per batch, hand the batch's work as an index into a table the context holds, not an Arc.
2. `done`: `bounded(pool.workers() + io + 1)`: at most that many tasks run at once (`self.running`), each sends once, so the channel never fills and never allocates after creation. `io`: bounded likewise (at most `running` IO jobs queue).
3. A test with blaze-alloc-count: once warm, a batch of N cached tasks through `Threads` allocates nothing per task (as blaze-graph's `a_warm_done_through_step_into_allocates_nothing`).
Semantics unchanged: same tasks, same order of sends per worker, same results.
